title: 25-year Amazon drought experiment reveals rainforest's vulnerability to extreme conditions
summary: The 25-year Esecaflor Project in Brazil's Amazon, which diverted 50% of rainwater from a one-hectare study area since 2001, shows significant die-off of large trees and potential transformation into a degraded forest ecosystem rather than savanna. The experimental structure was removed two years ago
takeaways: Duration: 25 years (started 2001); structure removed ~2 years ago (2024)
Method: 6,000 transparent plastic panels diverting ~50% rainfall for 2 decades
Outcome: significant large-tree die-off; forest shifted to new equilibrium (degraded forest, not savanna)
Longest-running, most extensive tropical forest drought study conducted
Monitoring: soil, air, tree growth, sap flow, roots; two 40-meter towers with NASA radar

title: Climate science declares 1.5C warming target unachievable; political consensus lacks acknowledgment

Despite this scientific consensus, leaders at COP31 in Turkey maintain political support for the target, invoking slogans like "keep 1.5 alive."
